title: NoisePQC++: A Unified NIST-Compliant PQC and Hybrid-PQC Implementation of the Noise Protocol
authors: Nadeem Ahmed, Aryya Gangopadhyay, Lei Zhang
abstract: The threat of quantum computers to classical public-key cryptography has created an urgent need to evolve secure communication protocols with post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) primitives. The Noise Protocol Framework, widely used in systems such as WireGuard and WhatsApp, traditionally relies on the Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) public-key exchange scheme, which is vulnerable to quantum threats. In this paper, we present NoisePQC++, a unified C++23 implementation of the Noise Protocol framework augmented with post-quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanisms and Hybrid Forward Secrecy. Our design integrates the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standardized ML-KEM algorithm alongside classical ECDH, enabling full PQC, hybrid ECDH+PQC handshakes, and unified support for all 57 classical Noise handshake pattern variants, 13 post-quantum Noise handshakes, and their hybrid variants. Compared with prior work, NoisePQC++ offers broader protocol coverage, more complete implementation support, and greater flexibility. Our evaluation shows minimal overhead under normal network conditions and acceptable overhead in adverse cases, while significantly improving resistance against quantum adversaries. These results indicate that NIST-standardized post-quantum and hybrid Noise handshakes are practical and provide a credible basis for future deployment.
summary: This paper addresses the cryptographic vulnerability posed by quantum computers to current key exchange methods used in protocols like Noise. The authors present NoisePQC++, a unified C++ implementation that integrates NIST-standardized Post-Quantum Cryptography (ML-KEM) with classical ECDH for hybrid security. Benchmarking confirms that these PQC and hybrid handshakes are computationally feasible, providing a practical path toward quantum-resistant secure communications.
main_problem: The urgent need to update secure communication protocols due to the looming threat quantum computers pose to classical public-key cryptography, specifically those relying on ECDH.
main_result: NoisePQC++ successfully implements unified C++23 support for classical, pure PQC, and hybrid Noise handshakes, proving that NIST-standardized post-quantum methods are practical for future deployment.
method: The authors developed a unified framework integrating lattice-based ML-KEM (NIST standard) with classical ECDH within the established Noise Protocol structure, using Hybrid Forward Secrecy.
model_or_system: The system models secure key exchange protocols based on the Noise Protocol Framework, which is used in modern messaging systems like WireGuard. The implementation uses C++23 and leverages cryptographic primitives from Botan.
key_observables: Handshake Latency (ML-KEM-768 vs X25519), CPU Time, Key/Ciphertext Sizes, Network Round-Trip Time (RTT), and Throughput Scaling ($	ext{hs/s}$).
important_parameters: Classical primitives include ECDH (e.g., X25519); PQC relies on ML-KEM based on the Module-LWE problem.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that serial mixing of shared secrets via HKDF chaining is sufficient for secure hybrid key derivation, and performance overheads are manageable for deployment.
figures_summary: Figures compare latency (Classical vs PQ vs HFS) across various Noise patterns; they also show CPU time comparisons and the significant increase in wire overhead due to larger PQC keys/ciphertexts.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the unified architecture of NoisePQC++, analyzes related work limitations, presents comprehensive benchmarking results across multiple metrics (latency, throughput), and concludes on feasibility for quantum-resistant channels.
